doc.name: A — outerwear catalogue, hands in frame, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: double-face wool coat
Category: outerwear
Shot programme: hands in frame
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this outerwear product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the top-down flat in a hands in frame treatment.

SUBJECT. A double-face wool coat. Lock the product itself to the reference — no proportional drift, no invented branding, no cleaned-up typography. Everything else in the frame is your design decision.

CAMERA. Directly overhead, product and props arranged on a single plane. Shoot on a 90mm tilt-shift at f/2, framing for rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-right.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with tungsten practicals in frame carrying the warm layer. Stage the product on or against book-matched marble, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a desaturated Nordic palette with cold blue shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
